subject: Clarify uptime / credits language in MSA + Order Form
messages:
From: Elena Park <epark@greengrid.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: GreenGrid Procurement <procurement@greengrid.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Jun 2029 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify uptime / credits language in MSA + Order Form

Hannah,

Thanks again for the demo last week — team is excited about Redwood's predictable latency and routing options. Legal and procurement reviewed the MSA/Order Form and have two areas where they need clearer language before we can move to signature: uptime measurement and aggregate credit cap.

Specific asks:
- How uptime is measured (region vs. global; rolling monthly window vs. calendar month).
- Whether cumulative service credits can exceed 30% of monthly fees (their procurement team is proposing a 20% cap).
- Maintenance windows: they want explicit blackout hours and advance notice timelines for planned maintenance.

I've attached our redline (GreenGrid_OrderForm_SLA_Redline_20290625.pdf) with inline questions. Can you share Redwood's preferred language and any legal pointers so we can close the loop this week?

Thanks,
Elena Park
Senior Procurement Manager
GreenGrid Inc.
procurement@greengrid.com

Attachment: GreenGrid_OrderForm_SLA_Redline_20290625.pdf (pdf, 127KB)

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Park <epark@greengrid.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Jun 2029 14:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify uptime / credits language in MSA + Order Form

Elena —

Appreciate the clear notes and the redline. I've read the attachment and sketched out Redwood's preferred positions below. I also attached a tracked-changes version from our side (Redwood_SLA_redline_hannah_v2.docx) with inline rationale. High-level summary:

- Uptime measurement: we measure per-region availability for region-specific purchases; for customers on multi-region routing we provide a weighted global availability metric. We prefer a rolling 30-day window for credit calculation (more representative of production behavior) — but we can accept calendar month if GreenGrid insists.

- Credit cap: standard offering is cumulative credits capped at 30% of monthly recurring charges (MRC) per billing period. We are willing to discuss a temporary 20% cap for the first two quarters as a commercial concession if GreenGrid commits to a 12-month term and a dedicated capacity minimum.

- Maintenance windows: standard maintenance (non-emergency) is scheduled with 72 hours notice and limited to two routine windows per month (each up to 90 minutes). Emergency maintenance is excluded from credits; planned maintenance during agreed blackout periods will be avoided. We can specify blackout hours for certain business-critical windows if provided in the Order Form appendix.

Next steps I propose:
1) Marissa (legal) to review the precise contract text for the uptime metric and credit cap.
2) If legal signs off, I can create an order-form addendum capturing the 12-month concession and dedicated capacity terms for the pricing team.
3) Quick sync call if GreenGrid wants to negotiate the maintenance blackout hours.

Are you available for a 20-minute call tomorrow (Wed) at 11am PT?

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
hannah_schmitt@redwoodinference.com
+1-415-555-0190

Attachment: Redwood_SLA_redline_hannah_v2.docx (docx, 89KB)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Elena Park <epark@greengrid.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 26 Jun 2029 09:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify uptime / credits language in MSA + Order Form

Hannah / Elena —

Thanks for the context. Quick legal read-through below; I included alternate text snippets you can drop directly into the MSA/Order Form. My comments:

1) Measurement and windowing
- Proposed text (drop-in): "Availability will be measured per Region unless explicitly stated otherwise in the Order Form. Availability will be calculated as the percentage of successful request-serving time over a rolling 30-day period, measured in UTC."
- Rationale: rolling 30-day avoids month-length edge cases and is industry common. We can change to calendar month if procurement requires it, but that will require explicit acceptance of month-end variance in signal.

2) Credit cap
- Proposed text (drop-in): "Cumulative service credits for any Billing Period shall not exceed thirty percent (30%) of the Monthly Recurring Charges for that Billing Period. Customer may request a temporary amendment to this cap as part of a written commercial addendum."
- Rationale: retains our standard exposure while allowing a path for one-off commercial concessions (documented). If you agree to a temporary 20% cap for Q1/Q2, we should convert that to a signed addendum referencing the Deal ID.

3) Maintenance windows and notice
- Proposed text (drop-in): "Planned maintenance shall be communicated at least seventy-two (72) hours in advance and limited to no more than two windows per calendar month (each window not to exceed ninety (90) minutes). Customer may designate up to two blackout windows per fiscal quarter in writing which Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to avoid."
- Note: "commercially reasonable efforts" preserves operational flexibility. If GreenGrid requires strict blackout guarantees, we need to scope Dedicated capacity and an escalation SLA.

Please see inline tracked changes in the attached docx. If GreenGrid accepts the addendum approach for the temporary credit cap, we should have procurement route a signature path (DocuSign) for the addendum only — keeps MSA clean.

I can join the call tomorrow at 11am PT. Lauren — can you weigh in on whether we should require dedicated capacity for strict blackout guarantees?

Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Contracts — Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com

Attachment: Redwood_SLA_redline_hannah_v2.docx (legal annotations)

From: Elena Park <epark@greengrid.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 30 Jun 2029 16:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify uptime / credits language in MSA + Order Form

Hannah / Marissa —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the suggested language. Procurement has reviewed Marissa's drop-in text and is broadly comfortable with the proposed rollover-to-addendum approach for the credit cap. Two final points before we prepare signatures:

- GreenGrid asks that the blackout windows be listed explicitly in the Order Form appendix (they will provide the two recurring weekly windows they need protected). Can Redwood commit to noting those hours and applying "commercially reasonable efforts" as Marissa suggested?
- For the concession (temporary 20% cap for Q1/Q2), procurement wants a milestone: GreenGrid will commit to a 12-month term and a minimum committed spend for dedicated capacity to qualify. Please confirm the eligibility threshold so we can include it in the addendum.

If you can send the final addendum text and the DocuSign routing tomorrow morning we can sign by EOD Friday. Appreciate the collaboration — looking forward to closing this out.

Best,
Elena
